2.1 Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

SECTION 2 CORPORATE PROFILE

2.1 Activities

Southern Copper Corporation, a New York Stock Exchange-listed company, is a leading global producer of copper and other metals, with operations centered in Mexico and Peru. Its core business activities encompass the exploration, mining, smelting, and refining of copper, alongside by-products such as molybdenum, zinc, silver, and gold, which are supplied to industries including construction, electronics, and renewable energy. The company's fastest-growing segments include copper production, fueled by rising demand from electric vehicles and infrastructure development, as well as molybdenum extraction for high-strength alloys in manufacturing. By focusing on operational efficiency and strategic investments in new projects, Southern Copper maintains a competitive edge in the global mining sector, emphasizing sustainable practices to support long-term growth. It is the largest Non ferrous metals sector company by market capitalization among NYSE- and TXSE-listed stocks.

The business conglomerate Fomento Económico (Femsa) and the bottler Coca-Cola Femsa, also known as KOF, have received reaffirmation of their long-term local credit rating from Fitch Ratings due to their business position and financial stability.

The New York-based rating agency confirmed the credit rating of Femsa and Coca-Cola Femsa at 'AAA(mex)', the highest level in the local investment-grade scale, while maintaining the outlook at 'stable'.

"The ratings reflect Femsa's robust position in the retail sector in Latin America and Europe across proximity, health, and fuel station segments," Fitch stated in a release.

The agency added that Coca-Cola Femsa's strong market share position is supported by an extensive and well-developed distribution network, the strong brand equity of Coca-Cola products, a diversified product portfolio, and robust execution at the point of sale.

"Fitch believes these factors provide a competitive advantage and enable the company to maintain leadership positions in its markets over the long term," the rating agency said in a statement.

Its core business centers on the operation, maintenance, and development of these facilities, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, aeronautical services, and non-aeronautical revenue streams such as retail, advertising, and parking. GAP has seen robust growth in passenger traffic, with international routes emerging as the fastest-growing segment, fueled by rising tourism and business travel demands. Additionally, cargo operations and commercial activities, particularly e-commerce-related logistics, have expanded rapidly, contributing to overall revenue diversification. This strategic focus on infrastructure upgrades and efficiency enhancements positions GAP as a key player in Mexico's aviation sector, supporting economic connectivity and sustainable growth. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 3rd largest Engineering & construction company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V.(NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR) (ASUR), a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the United States, and Colombia, today announced the call to assembly for its General Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting which will be held on January 26 th, 2026 and announced the agenda for the meeting. Press Release article 3 of 3, Source: WEC, 313 words

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. (ASUR) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a portfolio of 10 airports in the southeastern region, including the high-traffic Cancun International Airport. Its core business involves the operation, maintenance, and development of airport infrastructure, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, commercial concessions, and ancillary services like retail and parking. ASUR focuses on enhancing efficiency and passenger experience to support growing aviation demand. The company's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, fueled by tourism in destinations such as Cancun and the Riviera Maya, as well as non-aeronautical revenues from expanded retail and food services, which have seen robust increases due to rising traveler spending and airport expansions. This strategic emphasis has solidified ASUR's role in Mexico's aviation industry, contributing to economic connectivity and regional development. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 12th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste SAB de CV is the trade name used on the Mexico Stock Exchange and Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste S.A. de C.V. is used on the New York Stock Exchange.

Initially available in select Mexican markets, the Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle leverages the existing popularity of refillable formats. Jun 17, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Leverages Logistics-as-a-Service to Enhance Distribution

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. is quietly enhancing its distribution capabilities through Fomento Economico Mexicano's Logistics-as-a-Service offering. FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service fundamentally allows third-party brands to access the same warehousing, routing software, and last-mile fleet utilized by Coca-Cola in Mexico and other Latin American markets. Clients can seamlessly integrate into FEMSA's extensive delivery network, which significantly reduces the need for them to establish their own complex logistics operations. This means that consumer goods can be efficiently delivered to over 3 million points of sale, utilizing existing routes that serve thousands of small retail outlets daily.

For brands, especially those in the fast-moving consumer goods sector, this service provides an invaluable shortcut to market penetration. Products delivered alongside Coca-Cola benefit from the established distribution patterns that store owners are accustomed to, thus facilitating easier acceptance and integration into existing supply chains. The service's reach can substantially expedite market entry for new energy drinks or healthcare products, compressing lengthy rollout periods into mere months.

Technological infrastructure underpins this service, with advanced routing algorithms and inventory management tools ensuring efficient operations. FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service also offers clients features such as order tracking and delivery proof without necessitating additional investment in software. This is particularly crucial for pharmaceuticals and health products, where stringent temperature control and delivery reliability are essential.

Logistics-as-a-Service is a strategic component of FEMSA's broader vision to maximize value from its existing infrastructure. Although still a smaller segment compared to its core Coca-Cola bottling and OXXO retail operations, it represents a significant opportunity for growth. Investors should note that while immediate scale may be limited, the long-term potential for operating leverage in this logistics venture aligns with FEMSA's overarching objective of enhancing its distribution capabilities.

SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

SECTION 8 CORPORATE PROFILE

8.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

La fibra óptica en México es, desde hace años, uno de los ejes de la competencia en banda ancha, por lo que no es de extrañar que las grandes empresas del sector que cotizan en el mercado local – América Móvil, Megacable y Televisa – avancen en su despliegue.

Muestra de ello es la información que presentaron en el tercer trimestre de este año, en el que las tres emisoras de la Bolsa Mexicana de Valores (BMV) mostraron avances en sus respectivas estrategias.

Por ejemplo, América Móvil , el gigante de las telecomunicaciones de la familia Slim, reportó que al cierre del periodo que finalizó en septiembre, 94% de sus clientes ya se encuentran conectados mediante fibra óptica.

Respecto a la banda ancha en México, puedo adelantar que hemos mantenido un buen ritmo de crecimiento en los últimos trimestres", dijo Daniel Hajj, director general de la empresa, durante la llamada con analistas e inversionistas.

Aunque en la conversación los directivos de la empresa no detallaron cifras, los datos de América Móvil apuntan a que al cierre del trimestre los accesos de banda ancha en México ascendieron a 12.4 millones , lo que significó un avance de 4.8% en comparación con el mismo periodo de 2025.

Durante el trimestre, Telmex conectó 37,000 accesos nuevos de banda ancha en el trimestre, mientras que los ingresos en México crecieron 9.7% en la comparación anual.

Megacable sube a 89% de suscriptores con fibra óptica

Otra empresa que también mostró un avance en el despliegue de fibra óptica fue Megacable , que reportó que 89% de sus suscriptores estaban conectados mediante tecnología de fibra óptica. Esto significó un avance respecto al tercer trimestre de 2025, cuando el porcentaje se ubicó en 82%.

Al corte de septiembre de este año, los suscriptores de banda ancha de Megacable sumaron 6.07 millones , lo que representó un avance de 7.1% o 405,000 adiciones netas en la comparación anual.

Con ese porcentaje de penetración, la empresa se enfocará hacia adelante en áreas identificadas con alto potencial de crecimiento , de acuerdo con Raymundo Fernández, director general adjunto de la compañía.

Nos estamos centrando en la expansión en aquellas áreas donde existe un mayor potencial de crecimiento y donde, a nuestro juicio, aún queda un número considerable de kilómetros con presencia de solo dos operadores, ambos basados ??en fibra óptica", explicó a analistas e inversionistas.

A diferencia de América Móvil, Megacable proporciona otros detalles de su despliegue de fibra óptica, como los kilómetros que componen su red , y que a septiembre alcanzaron los 111,855 kilómetros.

Además, el número de casas pasadas con fibra hasta el hogar (FTTH, por sus siglas en inglés) alcanzó las 19.9 millones , un crecimiento de 6.4% respecto al cierre del tercer trimestre de 2025.

Televisa reconvierte su red a fibra óptica al hogar

Por su parte, Grupo Televisa también presentó avance en el despliegue de su red, solo que a diferencia de sus competidores, su medición se basa en su red , más que en el número de clientes.

Así, durante el trimestre incorporó 8,000 nuevas casas pasadas con fibra hasta el hogar, y al mismo tiempo reconvirtió a esta tecnología 1.3 millones de hogares que ya operaba pero mediante cable coaxial.

En lo que va de año, hemos actualizado más de 4.3 millones de hogares a la tecnología de fibra hasta el hogar (FTTH)", explicó Francisco Valim, director ejecutivo de Izzi, en la llamada con motivo del tercer trimestre.

La red de Televisa cuenta con más de 20.1 millones de casas , y el 67% de ellas ya cuenta con fibra óptica, añadió.

Los planes de la empresa son alcanzar el 100% de sus clientes con fibra hasta el hogar a mediados de 2027. Para el cierre de este año espera alcanzar el 75%.

Al corte de septiembre de este año, los suscriptores de banda ancha de Megacable sumaron 6.07 millones , lo que representó un avance de 7.1% o 405,000 adiciones netas en la comparación anual.

Con ese porcentaje de penetración, la empresa se enfocará hacia adelante en áreas identificadas con alto potencial de crecimiento , de acuerdo con Raymundo Fernández, director general adjunto de la compañía.

Nos estamos centrando en la expansión en aquellas áreas donde existe un mayor potencial de crecimiento y donde, a nuestro juicio, aún queda un número considerable de kilómetros con presencia de solo dos operadores, ambos basados ??en fibra óptica", explicó a analistas e inversionistas.

A diferencia de América Móvil, Megacable proporciona otros detalles de su despliegue de fibra óptica, como los kilómetros que componen su red , y que a septiembre alcanzaron los 111,855 kilómetros.

Además, el número de casas pasadas con fibra hasta el hogar (FTTH, por sus siglas en inglés) alcanzó las 19.9 millones , un crecimiento de 6.4% respecto al cierre del tercer trimestre de 2025.

Televisa reconvierte su red a fibra óptica al hogar

Por su parte, Grupo Televisa también presentó avance en el despliegue de su red, solo que a diferencia de sus competidores, su medición se basa en su red , más que en el número de clientes.

Así, durante el trimestre incorporó 8,000 nuevas casas pasadas con fibra hasta el hogar, y al mismo tiempo reconvirtió a esta tecnología 1.3 millones de hogares que ya operaba pero mediante cable coaxial.

En lo que va de año, hemos actualizado más de 4.3 millones de hogares a la tecnología de fibra hasta el hogar (FTTH)", explicó Francisco Valim, director ejecutivo de Izzi, en la llamada con motivo del tercer trimestre.

La red de Televisa cuenta con más de 20.1 millones de casas , y el 67% de ellas ya cuenta con fibra óptica, añadió.

Los planes de la empresa son alcanzar el 100% de sus clientes con fibra hasta el hogar a mediados de 2027. Para el cierre de este año espera alcanzar el 75%.

Optical Fiber in Mexico has been a key driver of competition in broadband for years, so it is not surprising that the major players in the sector listed on the local market – América Móvil, Megacable, and Televisa – are advancing in their infrastructure deployment.

This is evidenced by the information presented during the third quarter of this year, where all three companies listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange (BMV) reported progress in their respective strategies.

For instance, América Móvil , the telecommunications giant owned by the Slim family, reported that by the end of September, 94% of its customers were connected via fiber optic technology.

"Regarding broadband in Mexico, I can say that we have maintained a good growth rate in recent quarters," said Daniel Hajj, the company's CEO, during a call with analysts and investors.

Although the company's executives did not provide specific numbers during the conversation, América Móvil's data indicates that by the end of the quarter, broadband connections in Mexico reached 12.4 million , reflecting a 4.8% increase compared to the same period in 2025.

During the quarter, Telmex added 37,000 new broadband connections , while revenues in Mexico grew by 9.7% year-over-year.

Megacable Reaches 89% of Subscribers with Fiber Optic

Another company that showed progress in fiber optic deployment was Megacable , which reported that 89% of its subscribers were connected using fiber optic technology. This marked an increase from the third quarter of 2025, when the percentage stood at 82%.

As of September this year, Megacable's broadband subscribers totaled 6.07 million , representing a 7.1% gain or 405,000 net additions year-over-year.

With this penetration rate, the company plans to focus on areas identified as having high growth potential , according to Raymundo Fernández, the company's deputy general director.

"We are concentrating on expansion in areas where there is greater growth potential and where, in our opinion, there remains a significant number of kilometers with only two operators present, both based on fiber optics," he explained to analysts and investors.

Unlike América Móvil, Megacable provides additional details about its fiber optic deployment, including the kilometers that make up its network , which reached 111,855 kilometers by September.

Additionally, the number of homes passed with fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) reached 19.9 million , a growth of 6.4% compared to the end of the third quarter of 2025.

Televisa Converts Its Network to Fiber Optics for Homes

On its part, Grupo Televisa also reported progress in its network deployment; however, unlike its competitors, its measurement is based on its network rather than the number of customers.

During the quarter, it added 8,000 new homes passed with fiber-to-the-home, while simultaneously converted1.3 million homes that were already operational but using coaxial cable to this new technology.

This year, we have upgraded more than 4.3 million homes to fiber-to-the-home (FTTH) technology," explained Francisco Valim, executive director of Izzi, during the third-quarter earnings call.

Televisa's network encompasses more than 20.1 million homes , with 67% of them already equipped with fiber optics, he added.

The company's plans aim to achieve 100% coverage for its customers using fiber-to-the-home by mid-2027. By the end of this year, it expects to reach 75%.

About Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte, S.A.B. de C.V., together with its subsidiaries, holds concessions to develop, operate, and maintain airports in Mexico. It has a strategic alliance with VYNMSA Desarrollo Inmobiliario, S.A. de C.V. to build and operate an industrial park at the Monterrey airport. The company was founded in 1998 and is headquartered in Mexico City, Mexico.

It provides aeronautical services, which include passenger, aircraft landing and parking, passenger walkway, and airport security services. Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S. A. B. de C. V. was founded in 1996 and is headquartered in Mexico City, Mexico.

To mitigate risks in their investments including bankruptcy, insolvency, low levels of liquidity and inflated earnings, investors look at several key metrics and scores to assess each company. Below we include some of the analysis used to mitigate such risks.

Altman-Z score of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de

The Z-score formula for predicting bankruptcy was first published in 1968 by Professor Altman (Professor of Finance at New York University). The formula uses accounting ratios to predict whether a company could go bankrupt within two years with some studies showing it has an 80% accuracy rate for certain sectors. Some investors rely on it as a guide in assessing a company's financial strength and a way to mitigate risk, whereas others prefer different models that rely on market-based data instead. The score can also be useful to determine whether a company is heading in a positive or negative direction even though it may have zero risk of actual bankruptcy.

There are three variations of the Z-score and we have measured Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de with all three variations.

For the original Z-score bankruptcy model, Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de scores a Z = 0.66 for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025]; a deterioration from 0.91 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and 0.88 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024]. A Z score above >2.99 is considered "safe", a score between 1.81 and 2.99 is considered "grey" and a Z score under 1.81 is considered "distressed".

Solvency of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de

Debt to Equity Ratio of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is 1.34; a deterioration from 0.98 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and 1.07 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024].

Debt to Assets Ratio of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is 0.41; a deterioration from 0.40 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and steady from 0.41 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024].

Liquidity of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de

Cash Ratio of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is 0.34; a deterioration from 1.15 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and 0.51 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024]. This change in current ratio was driven by

- A decrease in current assets of MX$1.5 billion (or 27.2%) from the previous quarter and MX$224.8 million (or 5.2%) from year ago to MX$4.1 billion.

- An increase in current liabilities of MX$1.8 billion (or 58.3%) from the previous quarter and MX$1.5 billion (or 45.5%) from year ago to MX$4.8 billion.

Piotroski F-Score of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de has posted a mid-range Piotroski F-Score of 4 for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025], indicating a blend of strengths and weaknesses in its financial fundamentals. The Piotroski F-Score, which rates companies on a scale from 0 to 9 based on key fundamentals such as profitability, leverage, liquidity, and asset efficiency, is widely used by value investors to assess financial strength. A mixed score suggests that while Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de may be performing well in certain areas, such as cash flow or asset efficiency, it may also be facing challenges in others-highlighting the need for closer analysis by cautious investors.

Ohlson O-Score Summary

The Ohlson O-Score is a bankruptcy prediction that uses nine financial variables to estimate the probability of corporate financial distress within two years. The model outputs a score that is converted to a probability using logistic regression.

For the Period Ending 31 December, 2025, Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de scores an O = -8.4809

Based on the academic Ohlson model, scores below -1.80 indicate low bankruptcy risk, scores between -1.80 and 0 fall into the moderate-risk zone, and scores above 0 signal elevated financial distress.

To mitigate risks in their investments including bankruptcy, insolvency, low levels of liquidity and inflated earnings, investors look at several key metrics and scores to assess each company. Below we include some of the analysis used to mitigate such risks.

Altman-Z score of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de

The Z-score formula for predicting bankruptcy was first published in 1968 by Professor Altman (Professor of Finance at New York University). The formula uses accounting ratios to predict whether a company could go bankrupt within two years with some studies showing it has an 80% accuracy rate for certain sectors. Some investors rely on it as a guide in assessing a company's financial strength and a way to mitigate risk, whereas others prefer different models that rely on market-based data instead. The score can also be useful to determine whether a company is heading in a positive or negative direction even though it may have zero risk of actual bankruptcy.

There are three variations of the Z-score and we have measured Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de with all three variations.

For the original Z-score bankruptcy model, Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de scores a Z = 0.66 for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025]; a deterioration from 0.91 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and 0.88 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024]. A Z score above >2.99 is considered "safe", a score between 1.81 and 2.99 is considered "grey" and a Z score under 1.81 is considered "distressed".

Solvency of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de

Debt to Equity Ratio of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is 1.34; a deterioration from 0.98 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and 1.07 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024].

Debt to Assets Ratio of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is 0.41; a deterioration from 0.40 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and steady from 0.41 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024].

Liquidity of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de

Cash Ratio of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025] is 0.34; a deterioration from 1.15 in the previous quarter [Q1/2025] and 0.51 in the year-earlier period [Q2/2024]. This change in current ratio was driven by

- A decrease in current assets of MX$1.5 billion (or 27.2%) from the previous quarter and MX$224.8 million (or 5.2%) from year ago to MX$4.1 billion.

- An increase in current liabilities of MX$1.8 billion (or 58.3%) from the previous quarter and MX$1.5 billion (or 45.5%) from year ago to MX$4.8 billion.

Piotroski F-Score of Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de has posted a mid-range Piotroski F-Score of 4 for the quarter-ended 30 June 2025 [Q2/2025], indicating a blend of strengths and weaknesses in its financial fundamentals. The Piotroski F-Score, which rates companies on a scale from 0 to 9 based on key fundamentals such as profitability, leverage, liquidity, and asset efficiency, is widely used by value investors to assess financial strength. A mixed score suggests that while Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de may be performing well in certain areas, such as cash flow or asset efficiency, it may also be facing challenges in others-highlighting the need for closer analysis by cautious investors.

Ohlson O-Score Summary

The Ohlson O-Score is a bankruptcy prediction that uses nine financial variables to estimate the probability of corporate financial distress within two years. The model outputs a score that is converted to a probability using logistic regression.

For the Period Ending 31 December, 2025, Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro NorteB. de scores an O = -8.4809

Based on the academic Ohlson model, scores below -1.80 indicate low bankruptcy risk, scores between -1.80 and 0 fall into the moderate-risk zone, and scores above 0 signal elevated financial distress.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

5.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Through strategic investments in infrastructure and technology, OMA enhances operational efficiency and passenger experience, positioning itself as a vital player in Mexico's aviation sector. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 13th largest Airlines company by market capitalization.

SECTION 5 CORPORATE PROFILE

5.1 Activities

Arca Continental SAB de CV, a prominent Mexican conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages as a key franchise partner for The Coca-Cola Company. The company operates across Mexico, the United States, and South America, offering a diverse portfolio that includes carbonated soft drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and snacks. Its core activities encompass manufacturing, logistics, and sales through an extensive network of distribution channels, serving both retail and hospitality sectors. In recent years, the fastest-growing segments have been healthier beverage options, such as flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, driven by shifting consumer preferences toward wellness and hydration products. Additionally, international expansion into markets like Ecuador and Peru has fueled growth, enhancing revenue streams and market share. Arca Continental's strategic investments in sustainability and digital technologies further support its operational efficiency and long-term competitiveness in the global beverage industry. It is Mexico's largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

Arca Continental SAB de CV, a prominent Mexican conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages as a key franchise partner for The Coca-Cola Company. Additionally, international expansion into markets like Ecuador and Peru has fueled growth, enhancing revenue streams and market share. Arca Continental's strategic investments in sustainability and digital technologies further support its operational efficiency and long-term competitiveness in the global beverage industry. • "We must move faster," COP31 negotiations lead Australia says
  • COP31 goal: electrify more than a third of world economy by 2035
  • US shuns climate cooperation for second year in a row

Adds quote from Turkey President Erdogan in paragraph 10, replaces quote in final paragraph

By Simon Jessop and Tuvan Gumrukcu

ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 9 (Reuters) - Leaders of the COP31 climate summit urged the world to accelerate the fight against global warming amid rising temperatures and worsening climate-driven disasters, as the annual meeting began in Turkey on Monday.

The comments at the start of the two-week UN conference were an appeal to governments to focus on climate, even as other international crises from war to soaring inflation and the uncertainty of artificial intelligence compete for their attention.

"The urgency of this moment must drive us forward," UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell said at the opening of the event on Turkey's Mediterranean coast, adding that progress so far was "nowhere near fast enough."

A report by the United Nations Environment Programme published in October said the world was already poised to overshoot 1.5 degrees Celsius of warming above pre-industrial times, the threshold set at the 2015 Paris climate summit to avoid the worst consequences of warming.

This year is on track to be one of the four hottest on record, driven by a powerful El Nino, a UN report showed on Monday.

It has also stood out with a series of extreme heatwaves across Western Europe and a glacier collapse in Nepal that triggered a catastrophic flood killing more than 1,450 people, with thousands still missing.

Turkey's COP31 presidency has focused this year's summit on a goal to electrify more than a third of the global economy by 2035, up from around a fifth today. It is asking nations to sign onto a pledge supporting that target.

Theoretically, such a goal could help reduce planet-warming emissions by speeding the global shift away from fossil fuel-powered vehicles, furnaces, boilers, cooking stoves, and other greenhouse gas-emitting equipment.

"We want people to feel the results of climate talks in daily life: in buildings that use less energy, in clean public transport, in energy they can afford and in new jobs," Turkey's COP31 President Murat Kurum said.

But climate advocates have criticised the pledge because it does not require the additional electricity to come from low-carbon sources, setting up an early fight over whether electrification alone should count as climate progress.

Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan said he hoped Turkey could deliver concrete results.

"Our goal is to make this summit a platform where concrete results are produced, where countries turn their pledges into action, because it is no longer time to make promises that remain on paper," Erdogan told reporters on a return flight from Azerbaijan, according to a transcript of his comments shared by his office on Monday.

WAR AND TECH

The Iran war has underscored the world's attachment to fossil fuels, as has Russia's invasion of Ukraine, though some say the wars have also shown the benefits of moving to renewables.

Now in its ninth month, the Iran war has severely disrupted Middle East oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, lifting fuel prices around the globe and prompting a scramble for new supplies.

US President Donald Trump's administration — which is shunning climate talks for the second year running — has encouraged policies maximising oil, gas, and coal production to address the disruptions.

South Korea, India, Thailand and other Asian nations, meanwhile, have also increased their reliance on coal or taken steps to boost coal-fired power generation.

"A lot of people who previously might have been embarrassed to argue for continuing very high use of fossil fuel are now feeling empowered to make that case," said John Holdren of Harvard University, who was a science adviser to Barack Obama when he was US president.

At the same time, the deployment of renewable energy has also risen, driven by surging exports of cheap clean tech from China.

Stiell told the summit renewables were the clear answer to improving energy security.

"This year's fossil fuel cost chaos has delivered a global shockwave, hitting households hard and spreading inflation like a cancer," he said.

"But the solutions are clear," he added, saying renewable energy installations had already saved the global economy hundreds of billions of dollars.

The rapid rollout of AI is also complicating talks, driving a surge in global power demand and contributing to rising greenhouse gas emissions.

Turkey will call on governments, businesses and other institutions at COP31 to sign a pledge outlining principles to ensure AI is developed and deployed sustainably.

Chris Bowen, Australia's president of COP31 negotiations, said he hoped the conference would show the world that multilateralism works.

"Let's show future generations that this generation was equal to the moment, equal to the challenge," he said.

(Reporting by Ezgi Erkoyun, Tuvan Gumrukcu, Valerie Volcovici, Simon Jessop, and Sarah McFarlane; Writing by Richard Valdmanis; Editing by David Gregorio, Kate Mayberry and Jan Harvey)

(( Richard.valdmanis@thomsonreuters.com ))

Description: Nvidia said on Sunday (November 8) its board was probing whether CEO Jensen Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, after a media report alleged he had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing. Reuters Chief Technology Correspondent, Greater China Eduardo Baptista has more.
Short Link: https://lseg.group/4kHpemF

Video Transcript:

NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang has acknowledged to NVIDIA's board and all of its employees that he had an intimate relationship with the business executive. And this executive has been identified in media reports as Alice Huang, also known as "Huang Le." The more serious issue is not the affair itself, but rather the allegation in those reports that she was linked to a Chinese intelligence operation targeting him. NVIDIA says its board has opened an independent investigation into this reporting and the potential national security implications, and Jensen Huang has said that he would cooperate. It certainly is an unprecedented challenge to somebody that is seen as the key face of NVIDIA, and certainly somebody that has been instrumental to its rise. To put it simply, it clearly puts Huang under intense scrutiny. But it does not necessarily mean that he's about to lose his job. I think it all depends, really. On the one hand, he is NVIDIA's founder, chief executive, and central figure in its rise as the world's dominant supplier of AI chips, which are fundamental to the AI boom. But of course, the key question for the board will be whether its investigation concludes that there was any compromise of company information from Huang. And if it finds that there is no such impact, the board may conclude that continuity is more important for the company's interests. Of course, if there is a security lapse that is identified and the culprit is indeed Huang, the pressure on Huang would rise substantially. And this pressure would only increase if the investigation finds that Huang knowingly concealed this lapse. I think Washington would face a series of very difficult questions about who knew what, when they knew it, and what, if anything, they did with the information. Was Huang warned about this? Was NVIDIA warned? And did US officials assess whether sensitive commercial or even technological information could have been compromised? And there's a whole other dimension to this because NVIDIA's importance to US AI leadership and the export control tensions with China is so enormous that there could be questions about why there was no earlier public action or congressional notification.

I hope to have a great future here. NVIDIA has been coming to China for 30 years.

Remember that Jensen Huang is a vocal advocate for rolling back US export controls targeting Chinese access to NVIDIA's most cutting-edge AI chips. So, now, with this controversy, that advocacy will be seen in a much different light. And so, these are all questions for not just intelligence agencies, but also the Trump Administration, which has said publicly that it has been receptive to Jensen Huang's lobbying on this matter of US escort controls targeting China's access to NVIDIA chips. So, now that this whole debate has been intertwined with these underlying espionage allegations, it only remains to be seen how far NVIDIA's internal investigation will go and also how much congressional action will be taken against Huang and these allegations.

Dhaka

Dhaka, Nov. 9 -- As Bangladesh grapples with escalating violence and a deteriorating law-and-order situation, at least eight buses have been set ablaze and more than 50 crude bomb explosions rocked different locations across Dhaka over the past few days, according to a local media report.

It noted that a series of crude bomb explosions triggered panic at Dhaka University on Sunday evening, with multiple other locations across the capital also witnessing similar blasts.

The campus was still witnessing the evening rush when two loud explosions occurred in quick succession in the Teacher-Student Centre (TSC) area of Dhaka University.

Further blasts were reported near the administrative building, outside the VC Chattar and at the Mukti-Ganatantra Toron. Students also detained several people while they were attempting to flee the scene.

Meanwhile, crude bomb explosions were reported at several other locations across the capital, including outside the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) office in Malibagh, a report in Bangladeshi daily Dhaka Tribune stated.

The report further highlighted that in the early hours of Saturday, two motorcycle-borne individuals fled after detonating three to four crude bombs in quick succession at the Chowrasta intersection in the Jatrabari area of Dhaka.

Hours earlier, another bomb exploded outside the upazila parishad gate near Genda Bus Stand on the Dhaka-Aricha Highway in Savar, while eyewitnesses were unable to identify those responsible.

"Explosions are now occurring one after another across the capital and surrounding areas, in front of police stations, at police facilities, near important government buildings and on university campuses. Some attackers arrive on motorcycles, set off explosions and flee. In other cases, their movements are captured on CCTV. After each incident, police say they are investigating, conducting operations and trying to identify those responsible," the report mentioned.

"Questions remain, however, about who is behind the blasts and how directly the detained individuals are linked to them. Are police identifying and arresting the people who throw the bombs, or are arrests mainly of suspects and people accused of political affiliations, to fill arrest figures? And who is making and supplying the bombs, and directing the attacks?," it questioned,

Addressing the media at the DMP Media Centre on Sunday, Deputy Police Commissioner Md Akhtar Hossain said that police were closely monitoring incidents of crude bomb explosions and vehicle arson and conducting investigations into each of them.

Several suspects, including members of banned organisations and their affiliated outfits, have been taken into custody.

He said police suspected that a particular group was deliberately orchestrating sabotage activities to create panic among the public.

Speaking to Dhaka Tribune, Tawhidul Haque, a Dhaka University teacher and crime analyst, said that while arrests were essential to maintaining law and order, authorities must ensure that innocent people were not targeted and harassed merely on suspicion.

He stressed that no arrested person should be labelled a bomb thrower without sufficient evidence emerging from the investigation. Published by HT Digital Content Services with permission from IANS. For any query with respect to this article or any other content requirement, please contact Editor at contentservices@htdigital.in

Speaking to Dhaka Tribune, Tawhidul Haque, a Dhaka University teacher and crime analyst, said that while arrests were essential to maintaining law and order, authorities must ensure that innocent people were not targeted and harassed merely on suspicion.

He stressed that no arrested person should be labelled a bomb thrower without sufficient evidence emerging from the investigation. Published by HT Digital Content Services with permission from IANS. The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters.

By Mike Dolan

Nov 9 (Reuters) - A nervy tech sector starts the week with a nearly 4% slide in AI chip giant Nvidia on a bizarre tale of an extramarital affair and spying allegations.

Nvidia boss Jensen Huang admitted to employees that he'd had an affair with a woman who news reports claimed was spying for China. The company said it was investigating those allegations and Huang's position may now be in the balance.

As Huang is a central figure in the whole AI buildout and an industry power figure in relations with Washington and governments around the world, markets may now be pricing the risk of his removal.

President Trump's initial response was to give Huang the benefit of the doubt, but he too faces questions about reports that he didn't act when intelligence originally briefed him on the situation several months ago.

Either way, the story will not calm anxieties in the AI investment world, which has just suffered its worst week in well over a year despite Friday's relief rally. It may also simply play into the hands of Nvidia competitors such as AMD and other leading chipmakers.

Asia stocks followed Friday's Wall Street tech bounce with gains of their own on Monday.

Markets were also digesting Friday's strong US payrolls report, where broad-based job gains came in at twice forecasts and lifted the three-month average payroll gain to more than 130,000 per month. Bets on another Federal Reserve interest rate rise next month pushed higher as a result.

Elsewhere, oil prices slipped on Monday after Trump indicated at the weekend that there would be no immediate re-escalation of the Iran conflict - a decision that follows the Republican Party's heavy defeats in last week's midterm elections.

In the background, Israeli opposition parties under Gadi Eisenkot have been given the first chance to form a government following the recent inconclusive elections there.

In China, there was a mixed picture on October inflation, with producer price inflation accelerating strongly but consumer price gains slipping back once more.

Otherwise, the release of US consumer price inflation data on Tuesday will top the economic release calendar this week as the earnings season starts to wind down.

CHART OF THE DAY

Nvidia shares fell sharply on Monday after news of the probe into Jensen Huang, which has put a spotlight on his future given Nvidia's status as the world's most valuable chipmaker and the CEO's role as the most prolific salesman of the AI boom.

TODAY'S EVENTS TO WATCH

  • US 3-year note auction (1 p.m. EST)

  • Fed's Michelle Bowman, Chicago Fed's Austan Goolsbee and Richmond Fed's Thomas Barkin speak
